# **Abstract**

The increasing adoption of digital commerce has created new opportunities for small businesses and entrepreneurs, while also introducing significant operational challenges related to production, branding, logistics, and market visibility. This project presents Talentree, an intelligent digital platform designed not only as a multi-vendor e-commerce marketplace, but also as an integrated business support ecosystem for business owners and emerging brands.

Talentree provides business owners with a centralized platform to manage and grow their businesses through a wide range of services. In addition to enabling online product showcasing and sales, the system supports raw material sourcing, packaging services, shipping and logistics coordination, branding and marketing assistance, business development guidance, and production requests that connect business owners with manufacturing vendors capable of producing their products. This creates a complete digital environment that supports businesses from product creation to customer delivery.

The system was developed using a modern full-stack architecture consisting of an Angular frontend, ASP.NET Core Web API backend, SQL Server database, and integrated AI-powered analytics services. The platform serves three primary user roles: customers, business owners, and administrators.

**User Roles**

To improve platform intelligence and decision-making, several Artificial Intelligence modules were integrated, providing personalized recommendations, operational insights, and data-driven support for both administrators and business owners: 

The platform emphasizes scalability, maintainability, security, and responsive user experience through layered architecture, RESTful APIs, JWT authentication, SignalR real-time communication, and modern UI/UX practices. Extensive testing and validation were conducted to ensure system reliability, performance, and usability. 

Talentree demonstrates how modern web technologies and intelligent systems can be combined to create a comprehensive digital business ecosystem that empowers entrepreneurs, supports business growth, simplifies operational processes, and enhances customer engagement within a unified platform. 

---

أدّى التوسّع المتزايد في اعتماد التجارة الرقمية (digital commerce) إلى خلق فرص جديدة أمام أصحاب المشاريع الصغيرة ورواد الأعمال، في حين فرض في الوقت نفسه تحديات تشغيلية جوهرية مرتبطة بالإنتاج، وبناء الهوية التجارية (branding)، والخدمات اللوجستية، وظهور المنتجات أمام السوق. يقدّم هذا المشروع منصة Talentree، وهي منصة رقمية ذكية لا تقتصر على كونها سوقًا إلكترونيًا متعدد البائعين (multi-vendor e-commerce marketplace)، بل تمثّل أيضًا منظومة متكاملة لدعم الأعمال لصالح أصحاب المشاريع والعلامات التجارية الناشئة.

توفّر Talentree لأصحاب الأعمال منصة مركزية لإدارة أعمالهم وتنميتها من خلال مجموعة واسعة من الخدمات. فإلى جانب عرض المنتجات والبيع عبر الإنترنت، يدعم النظام توفير المواد الخام، وخدمات التغليف، وتنسيق الشحن والخدمات اللوجستية، والمساعدة في التسويق وبناء العلامة التجارية، والإرشاد في تطوير الأعمال، وكذلك طلبات الإنتاج التي تربط أصحاب الأعمال بموردين قادرين على تصنيع منتجاتهم. وبذلك تُشكَّل بيئة رقمية متكاملة تواكب المشروع منذ لحظة إنتاج المنتج وحتى تسليمه للعميل.

طُوِّر النظام باستخدام معمارية full-stack حديثة تتكوّن من واجهة أمامية (frontend) مبنية بتقنية Angular، وخلفية (backend) مبنية بـ ASP.NET Core Web API، وقاعدة بيانات SQL Server، إلى جانب خدمات تحليلات مدعومة بالذكاء الاصطناعي (AI). وتخدم المنصة ثلاثة أدوار رئيسية للمستخدمين: العميل، وصاحب النشاط التجاري، ومسؤول النظام (admin).

يمكن للعميل تصفّح المنتجات، واستكشاف العلامات التجارية، وإدارة قائمة الرغبات، وتنفيذ الطلبات، ومتابعة الشحنات. أما صاحب النشاط التجاري فيستطيع إدارة منتجاته، ومتابعة المبيعات، وطلب خدمات الأعمال، والتواصل مع الموردين، والوصول إلى لوحات تحليلات ذكية (AI dashboards). في حين يتولّى مسؤول النظام الإشراف على تشغيل المنصة، ومراجعة المنتجات، وإدارة المستخدمين، وأنظمة الدعم، والتقارير التحليلية.

ولتحسين ذكاء المنصة وجودة اتخاذ القرار، تم دمج عدّة وحدات ذكاء اصطناعي، من بينها أنظمة التوصية (recommendation systems)، والتنبؤ بالمبيعات (sales forecasting)، وتحليل المشاعر (sentiment analysis)، وتقسيم العملاء (customer segmentation)، وكشف الحالات الشاذة (anomaly detection)، والذكاء المتعلق بإدارة المخزون (inventory intelligence)، وتقييم جودة المنتج. وتوفّر هذه القدرات توصيات مخصّصة، ورؤى تشغيلية، ودعمًا مبنيًا على البيانات لكل من مسؤولي المنصة وأصحاب الأعمال.

وتُركّز المنصة على قابلية التوسّع (scalability)، وسهولة الصيانة، والأمان، وتجربة مستخدم متجاوبة، وذلك من خلال تطبيق معمارية طبقية (layered architecture)، وواجهات برمجية من نوع RESTful APIs، والمصادقة عبر JWT، والاتصال الفوري باستخدام SignalR، إلى جانب أفضل ممارسات تصميم واجهة وتجربة المستخدم الحديثة (UI/UX). كما أُجريت اختبارات وتحقّقات موسّعة لضمان موثوقية النظام وأدائه وسهولة استخدامه.

وتُظهر Talentree كيف يمكن للتقنيات الحديثة للويب والأنظمة الذكية أن تتكامل لتشكيل منظومة أعمال رقمية شاملة تُمكِّن رواد الأعمال، وتدعم نمو المشاريع، وتُبسّط العمليات التشغيلية، وتُعزّز تفاعل العملاء ضمن منصة موحّدة واحدة.

# **CHAPTER 1: Introduction**

**\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

## **1.1 Project Overview**

The rapid advancement of digital technologies has transformed the way businesses operate and interact with customers. E-commerce platforms have become essential tools for businesses to expand their reach, improve operational efficiency, and provide better customer experiences. However, many small and emerging businesses still face major challenges beyond simply selling products online — sourcing raw materials, finding manufacturing support, managing packaging and shipping, building brand identity, and accessing marketing and business development services.

To address these challenges, this project introduces Talentree, an intelligent business support and multi-vendor marketplace platform designed to empower entrepreneurs and small business owners through an integrated digital ecosystem. The platform not only enables online product selling and customer interaction but also provides additional operational and business growth services that support businesses throughout their entire lifecycle.

Talentree allows business owners to showcase products, manage orders, communicate with customers, monitor sales analytics, and request specialized services such as branding, marketing support, packaging, logistics, and production assistance. The platform also enables business owners to submit manufacturing requests and connect with manufacturing vendors capable of producing products according to required specifications.

Customers can browse products, explore brands, search and filter items, manage wishlists, place orders securely, and track shipments through a user-friendly interface. Administrators oversee platform operations including product moderation, seller approval, complaint handling, financial monitoring, and system analytics.

The system was developed using modern web technologies including Angular for frontend development, ASP.NET Core Web API for backend services, SQL Server for database management, and AI-powered analytics modules for intelligent recommendations and business insights.

---

## **1.2 Problem Statement**

Many small business owners and startup brands struggle to establish and grow their businesses due to the lack of centralized platforms that combine e-commerce capabilities with operational support services. Traditional e-commerce systems mainly focus on product selling and purchasing while ignoring critical business requirements such as manufacturing support, supplier communication, branding assistance, packaging services, logistics coordination, and business growth guidance.

Additionally, business owners often rely on multiple disconnected platforms and service providers to manage different operational activities, leading to inefficiency, communication difficulties, increased costs, and poor business scalability.

Customers also face challenges in discovering trustworthy local brands, receiving personalized recommendations, and interacting with businesses through engaging and intelligent shopping experiences.

Therefore, there is a need for a comprehensive digital platform that integrates e-commerce functionality with intelligent business support services and AI-driven analytics to improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experience, and support sustainable business growth.

---

**1.3 Project Objectives**

The main objective of Talentree is to develop a smart and scalable digital platform that supports both customers and business owners through integrated e-commerce and business services. The project aims to achieve the following objectives:

* Develop a multi-vendor marketplace platform for product browsing and online purchasing.  
* Provide business owners with tools for managing products, orders, and customer interactions.  
* Enable access to operational services such as packaging, shipping, branding, and marketing support.  
* Create a production request system that connects business owners with manufacturing vendors.  
* Implement intelligent recommendation systems for customers and business owners.  
* Provide AI-powered analytics and forecasting tools for administrators and sellers.  
* Ensure secure authentication and authorization using modern security practices.  
* Deliver a responsive and user-friendly interface across multiple devices.  
* Improve platform efficiency through real-time notifications and automated workflows.

---

## **1.5 Proposed Solution**

Talentree provides an integrated solution that combines marketplace functionality with business support services within a single platform. Instead of relying on multiple disconnected systems, business owners can manage operations, communicate with vendors, access support services, and sell products from one centralized environment.

The platform utilizes modern web technologies and Artificial Intelligence modules to deliver intelligent recommendations, predictive analytics, customer segmentation, sentiment analysis, and operational insights. Real-time communication and notification systems improve responsiveness and user engagement, while secure payment integration ensures reliable financial transactions.

By combining e-commerce capabilities with operational and manufacturing support services, Talentree creates a comprehensive ecosystem that supports entrepreneurs and enhances business scalability.

---

## **1.6 Target Users**

The platform is designed for several categories of users:

Customers — Individuals who browse products, place orders, interact with brands, and purchase products online.

Business Owners — Entrepreneurs and small business owners seeking digital tools for selling products, managing operations, and growing their businesses.

Manufacturing Vendors — Service providers and manufacturers who receive production requests and collaborate with business owners to produce products.

## **1.8 Development Methodology**

The project followed an iterative and modular development methodology. System requirements were analyzed and divided into functional modules including frontend, backend, AI services, and administrative systems. The development process included:

* Requirement analysis  
* System design and architecture planning  
* UI/UX design  
* Frontend implementation  
* Backend and database development  
* AI module integration  
* Testing and validation  
* Deployment and optimization

This methodology allowed gradual system enhancement, easier debugging, and efficient team collaboration.

# **Chapter 2: System Analysis & Requirements**

This chapter presents the analysis of the Talentree platform's requirements, derived from the project's Software Requirements Specification (SRS). It defines what the system must do (functional requirements), the quality attributes it must satisfy (non-functional requirements), the actors who interact with it and their permissions, the core use cases, the governing business rules, the constraints shaping the design, and a feasibility assessment confirming the project is viable within its available resources and timeline.

**2.1 Functional Requirements**

Functional requirements describe the concrete capabilities the system must provide to each user type. They are organized into four modules — Business Owner, Customer, Admin, and AI & Recommendation System — and individually identified using the format FR-XX-YY (module code and sequence number), each tagged with a priority level of Critical, High, Medium, or Low. In total the SRS defines 37 Business Owner, 21 Customer, 47 Admin, and 21 AI requirements (126 overall). To keep this chapter readable, the tables below list only the Critical/High-priority, representative requirements of each module; the complete requirement-by-requirement specification (inputs, processing, outputs, acceptance criteria) is provided in the appendix.

**2.3 User Roles & Permissions**

The platform defines four user roles, each with a distinct scope of access, described in Table 2.3 and detailed further in Table 2.4.

**Role Overview**

* **Customer:** browses and purchases products, manages personal orders, wishlist, and reviews.

* **Business Owner:** manages product catalog and orders, sources raw materials as a buyer, tracks finances, and uses AI assistance.

* **Administrator:** approves sellers and products, resolves disputes, manages vendors, and monitors platform health.

* **Super Administrator:** holds full system privileges, including managing other admin accounts, RBAC policy, and audit logs.

2.6 System Constraints  
2.6.1 Technical Constraints

* Backend must be built with ASP.NET Core; frontend with Angular; database with Microsoft SQL Server.  
* AI services must be Python-based and exposed via API.  
* Payment processing limited to Stripe for the MVP; real-time features must use SignalR.

2.6.2 Business Constraints

* MVP supports only three business categories (Fashion & Accessories, Handmade Crafts, Natural & Beauty Products).  
* Arabic language support and native mobile apps are deferred to Phase 2\.  
* The platform must comply with Egyptian e-commerce and data-protection regulations regarding pricing transparency, user privacy, and secure payments.

2.6.3 Security Constraints

* All data transmission must use HTTPS.  
* Passwords must be hashed with an industry-standard algorithm (bcrypt).  
* Payment card information must never be stored on platform servers.

2.7 Feasibility Study  
The feasibility of the Talentree MVP was assessed across four standard dimensions, summarized in Table 2.5 and detailed below.

**Table 2.7 — Feasibility Assessment Summary**

**![][image12]**

2.7.1 Technical Feasibility

The chosen stack — ASP.NET Core, Angular, SQL Server, and Python-based AI microservices — is mature, well-documented, and matches the team's existing skill distribution across Backend, Frontend, and AI/Data Science sub-teams. Development and demo hosting on Render, with a planned migration to Azure for production, keeps infrastructure setup lightweight during the academic timeline while leaving a clear path to a scalable cloud deployment. The project is judged **technically feasible**.

2.7.2 Economic Feasibility

As a graduation project, Talentree relies primarily on free or low-cost resources: open-source frameworks, free-tier hosting for development, and Stripe's pay-as-you-go pricing model with no upfront integration cost. No specialized hardware is required beyond standard development machines. The project is judged **economically feasible** within a student budget.

2.7.3 Operational Feasibility

The defined roles, approval workflows, and support/complaint tools give administrators the operational control needed to keep the marketplace safe and trustworthy from launch. The three targeted user classes have clearly scoped technical expertise levels (low-to-medium for Customers and Business Owners, high for Admins), and the interface is designed to match, which supports smooth day-to-day operation once deployed. The project is judged **operationally feasible**.

2.7.4 Schedule Feasibility

Scope is deliberately bounded for the MVP: three business categories, a single payment gateway, and deferred features such as messaging, native mobile apps, and multi-language support are pushed to Phase 2\. This focused scope, combined with success metrics tied to post-hosting milestones (50+ business owners, 500+ customers, 200+ transactions), keeps the project achievable within the graduation timeline. The project is judged **feasible on schedule**.

**Conclusion:** across all four dimensions, the Talentree MVP is assessed as feasible, provided the Phase 2 scope items remain out of bounds for the current release.

# **Chapter 4: Frontend Development**

---

## 4**.1 Frontend Overview**

The frontend of the system represents the presentation layer that directly interacts with end users. It is responsible for rendering the user interface, handling user inputs, and providing a responsive and interactive experience. The frontend serves as the bridge between users and the backend services, ensuring smooth communication and real-time data visualization.

In this project, the frontend is implemented using Angular, following a Single Page Application (SPA) architecture. This approach enables dynamic content updates without requiring full page reloads,This leads to an improved user experience and increased speed of interaction with the system.

The frontend is designed to support multiple user roles, where each role is provided with a customized interface and functionality based on its permissions. These interfaces include dashboards, forms, data views, and interactive components that allow users to perform system operations efficiently.

From a functional perspective, the frontend is responsible for:

* Capturing and validating user input  
* Communicating with backend APIs using HTTP requests  
* Displaying data retrieved from the server  
* Managing application state and user sessions  
* Providing feedback through notifications, alerts, and error messages

Additionally, the frontend is built using a modular and component-based architecture, which enhances code reusability, maintainability, and scalability. Each feature is implemented as an independent component, allowing easier development, testing, and future extensions.

The communication between the frontend and backend is handled through RESTful APIs, where data is exchanged in JSON format. This decoupled architecture ensures flexibility, as the frontend can evolve independently from the backend while maintaining consistent functionality.

Overall, the frontend plays a critical role in delivering a seamless user experience, ensuring that system functionalities are accessible, efficient, and easy to use.

## 

## 4**.2 Introduction to Angular Framework**

![][image13]

Angular is a modern, open-source frontend framework developed by Google for building dynamic and scalable web applications. It is widely used for developing Single Page Applications (SPAs), where content is dynamically updated without requiring full page reloads.

Angular is built using TypeScript, a statically typed superset of JavaScript, which enhances code quality, maintainability, and scalability. The framework provides a structured and opinionated approach to application development, making it particularly suitable for large-scale and enterprise-level systems.

One of the core features of Angular is its component-based architecture. In this approach, the user interface is divided into independent and reusable components. Each component consists of:

* A template (HTML) that defines the UI  
* A class (TypeScript) that controls logic  
* Styles (CSS) that define appearance

This structure promotes modularity and simplifies development and maintenance.

Angular also provides a comprehensive set of built-in features, including:

* A powerful routing system for navigation between views  
* Reactive and template-driven forms for handling user input  
* HTTP client for communication with backend APIs  
* Dependency injection for managing services and application logic

Additionally, Angular uses reactive programming principles through RxJS, enabling efficient handling of asynchronous data streams such as API responses.

Another key advantage of Angular is its support for performance optimization techniques such as Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compilation and lazy loading. These features help reduce application load time and improve overall performance.

In this project, Angular was selected as the frontend framework due to its scalability, modular structure, and rich ecosystem, which align with the requirements of building a maintainable and high-performance web application.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

## 4**.3 Frontend Architecture**

The frontend of the system is designed using a modern, scalable architecture based on the Single Page Application (SPA) model. This architecture separates the presentation layer from the backend logic, enabling independent development, improved maintainability, and enhanced user experience.

In this project, Angular is used as the core framework to implement a modular and component-based architecture. The application is structured into clearly defined layers, each responsible for a specific functionality, ensuring separation of concerns and clean code organization.

---

### **4.3.1 Single Page Application (SPA) Architecture**

The system follows the SPA approach, where the entire application is loaded once, and subsequent interactions dynamically update the content without full page reloads.

This approach provides:

* Faster navigation between views  
* Reduced server load  
* Improved user experience

User interactions trigger HTTP requests to the backend API, and the frontend updates the UI dynamically based on the received data.

---

### **4.3.2 Component-Based Architecture**

Angular divides the application into reusable and independent components. Each component represents a specific part of the user interface and consists of:

* Template (HTML) for structure  
* TypeScript class for logic  
* CSS for styling

This modular design allows:

* Reusability of UI elements  
* Easier testing and debugging  
* Simplified maintenance and scalability

---

### **4.3.3 Layered Architecture**

The frontend is organized into multiple logical layers to ensure clear separation of responsibilities:

#### **🔹 Presentation Layer**

Responsible for rendering the user interface and handling user interactions through Angular components and templates.

#### **🔹 Application Layer**

Contains business logic and application rules implemented within services. It processes data and coordinates between components and external APIs.

#### **🔹 Data Access Layer**

Handles communication with the backend using Angular HTTP client. It is responsible for sending requests and receiving responses from RESTful APIs.

---

### **4.3.4 Communication with Backend**

The frontend communicates with the backend through RESTful APIs using HTTP requests. Data is exchanged in JSON format, ensuring lightweight and efficient communication.

The process includes:

1. User performs an action in the UI  
2. Angular service sends an HTTP request  
3. Backend processes the request  
4. Response is returned to the frontend  
5. UI is updated dynamically

---

### **4.3.5 Modular Structure**

The application is divided into feature modules, each representing a specific domain or functionality. This modular structure improves scalability and enables lazy loading, where modules are loaded only when needed.

Examples of modules include:

* Authentication module  
* User management module  
* Dashboard module

---

### **4.3.6 Key Architectural Benefits**

The chosen frontend architecture provides several advantages:

* Scalability for large applications  
* High maintainability through modular design  
* Reusability of components  
* Improved performance using SPA techniques  
* Clear separation between frontend and backend

## 4**.4 Frontend Structure (Module-Based Architecture)**

![][image14]

The frontend of the system is developed using Angular and follows a module-based architecture. This approach enhances scalability, maintainability, and separation of concerns by organizing the application into independent feature modules. Each module represents a specific domain or user role and contains its own pages, components, and core functionalities.

---

### **4.4.1 Admin Module**

The Admin module is responsible for managing administrative functionalities within the system. It contains several pages, including Admin, Admin Home, Dashboard, Business Owner, Suppliers, and Raw Material. * Top Navigation Bar  
* Table Component  
* Modal Card  
* Pagination  
* Status Page  
* Search Filter

The module also contains a core folder that includes services, pipes, and interfaces specific to the admin functionality.

---

### **4.4.2 Business Owner Module**

The Business Owner module handles all functionalities related to business owners. It includes pages such as Production Request, Notifications, Business Owner Home, Orders, Raw Material, and Settings. Each page contains its own set of components and logic.

Similar to the Admin module, it provides reusable components including:

* Side Navigation  
* Top Navigation  
* Table Component  
* Modal Card  
* Pagination  
* Status Page  
* Search Filter

This module also includes a core folder containing services, pipes, and interfaces relevant to business owner operations.

---

### **4.4.3 Authentication Module**

The Authentication module is responsible for user authentication and account management. It includes pages such as:

* Login  
* Register  
* Register Business Owner  
* Google Login  
* Facebook Login  
* Email Verification

This module focuses on handling authentication workflows and user access control.

---

### **4.4.4 Customer Module**

The Customer module is dedicated to handling customer-related features and interactions. It is designed to include pages and components specific to customer functionality. This module can be extended in future development phases.

---

### **4.4.5 Public Module**

The Public module contains publicly accessible pages that do not require authentication. These include:

* Landing Page  
* About  
* Testimonials  
* Offers  
* Contact

It also includes reusable components such as:

* Public Navigation Bar  
* Footer

Like other modules, it contains a core folder for services, pipes, and interfaces.

---

### **4.4.6 Core Structure (Module-Level and Global Core)**

Each feature module includes its own core folder that encapsulates:

* Services  
* Pipes  
* Interfaces

In addition, a global Core module is defined at the root level of the application. This global core contains shared services and route guards that are used across the entire application.

The guards include:

* Authentication Guard (Auth Guard)  
* Role-Based Guard  
* Guest Guard

These guards are responsible for controlling access to routes based on authentication status and user roles.

### **4.4.7 Layouts**

The application defines multiple layout components to support different user roles and sections of the system. These layouts include:

* Admin Layout

Each layout provides a consistent structure (navigation, header, and content area) for its corresponding module.

### **4.4.8 Global Styling**

### **4.4.9 Summary**

This modular frontend structure ensures that the application is well-organized, scalable, and easy to maintain. By isolating features into independent modules and centralizing shared functionalities, the system becomes more flexible and extensible for future enhancements.

## 4**.5 Architecture Design Choice: Module-Based vs Component-Based**

In Angular applications, different architectural approaches can be used to organize the frontend structure. Two common approaches are component-based organization and module-based architecture.

While Angular inherently uses components as the building blocks of the user interface, this project adopts a module-based architecture as the primary organizational strategy.

---

### **Component-Based Approach**

The component-based approach focuses on building the application as a collection of independent UI components. Each component encapsulates its own template, logic, and styling.

Although this approach promotes reusability and simplicity, it becomes difficult to manage as the application grows, especially in large-scale systems with multiple features and user roles.

---

### **Module-Based Approach**

The module-based architecture organizes the application into feature modules, where each module represents a specific domain or functionality (e.g., Admin, Business Owner, Authentication).

Each module contains:

* Pages (components)  
* Reusable components  
* Services and business logic  
* Interfaces and utilities

This structure allows better separation of concerns and improves scalability.

---

### **Why Module-Based Architecture Was Selected**

The module-based approach was chosen for this project for several reasons:

* Scalability: The system includes multiple roles and complex features, requiring clear separation between domains  
* Maintainability: Each module can be developed, tested, and maintained independently  
* Code Organization: Related functionalities are grouped together, making the codebase easier to navigate  
* Lazy Loading Support: Modules can be loaded only when needed, improving performance  
* Team Collaboration: Different modules can be developed simultaneously by different developers

**Module-Based vs Component-Based Organization** 

The following table summarizes the key differences between module-based and component-based organization approaches. 

| Aspect | Module-Based Architecture | Component-Based Approach |
| ----- | ----- | ----- |
| **Focus** | Organizing the application by features or domains | Building the UI using reusable components |
| **Structure Level** | High-level (application structure) | Low-level (UI elements) |
| **Scalability** | Highly scalable for large applications | Limited scalability when used alone |
| **Code Organization** | Groups related components, services, and logic in one module | Components are organized individually without clear domain separation |
| **Maintainability** | Easier to maintain due to clear separation of concerns | Becomes harder to manage as the application grows |
| **Reusability** | Reusability within modules and across shared modules | High reusability of individual UI components |
| **Team Collaboration** | Teams can work on different modules independently | Collaboration is harder without clear boundaries |
| **Performance** | Supports lazy loading for better performance | Does not directly support lazy loading |
| **Best Use Case** | Large, complex applications with multiple features | Small to medium applications or UI-focused parts |
| **Angular Role** | Defines application structure using NgModules | Defines UI using components |

Based on this comparison, the module-based architecture was selected to ensure better scalability, maintainability, and clear separation of application features.

# **4.6 State Management Strategy (with Implementation Examples)**

State management refers to how an application stores, updates, and shares data between different parts of the frontend. In modern Single Page Applications (SPAs) such as those built with Angular, managing state efficiently is essential to ensure consistency, performance, and maintainability as the application grows.

---

##  4**.6.1 What is “State” in a Frontend Application?**

State represents any data that can change during the lifecycle of the application, such as:

* User information (logged-in user, roles, profile data)  
* UI state (loading indicators, modal visibility, form status)  
* Business data (lists of items, dashboard statistics, API results)

In Angular applications, state exists at different levels:

* **Component state** → local to a single component  
* **Shared state** → used across multiple components  
* **Global state** → application-wide data such as authentication

  ## 4**.6.5 Reactive State with RxJS (Code Example)**

Angular uses RxJS to handle asynchronous data streams.

### **Key concepts:**

* Observable → stream of data  
* BehaviorSubject → stores and emits current state  
* Subscription → listens to updates

  ### **Example (State Management Service Pattern)**

  `private dataSubject = new BehaviorSubject<any>(null);`  
  `data$ = this.dataSubject.asObservable();`  
    
  `setData(data: any) {`  
   `this.dataSubject.next(data);`  
  `}`

This ensures that whenever data changes, all subscribed components are automatically updated.

3. Data is stored in BehaviorSubject (if shared state)  
4. All subscribed components receive updates instantly

# CHAPTER 5: Backend Development

**\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_**

## 5.1 Backend Overview

The Talentree backend serves as the core engine of the platform, orchestrating business logic, data persistence, authentication, real-time communication, and external service integration. Built with **ASP.NET Core 8.0**, the backend follows enterprise-grade architectural patterns — specifically Onion Architecture — to ensure scalability, maintainability, and testability across all platform modules.

The backend exposes a comprehensive RESTful API consumed by two distinct frontends: the Business Owner portal and the Customer marketplace. A dedicated Admin Dashboard module is layered on top, giving platform administrators fine-grained control over users, products, financial operations, content, and AI-driven analytics — all protected by role-based authorization and a full audit trail.

Core Responsibilities

* **Business Logic Enforcement:** Validates rules such as one-pending-payout-per-BO, material basket constraints, and production request approval workflows.  
* **Data Management:** Manages 52+ entities spanning authentication, business owner operations, raw material procurement, production requests, financial ledger, customer orders, and notifications.  
* **API Gateway:** Exposes 80+ RESTful endpoints organized by functional domain and role, documented via Swagger/OpenAPI.  
* **Admin Dashboard:** Dedicated controller layer giving admins full control over platform governance including user moderation, product approval, payout processing, content management, and AI analytics proxy.  
* **Real-Time Communication:** Delivers instant notifications via SignalR for order updates, quote approvals, production status changes, and system alerts.  
* **External Integration:** Coordinates with Stripe for payment processing, RabbitMQ for asynchronous event-driven communication, and a FastAPI AI microservice for predictive analytics.  
* **Security Layer:** Implements JWT-based authentication with refresh token rotation, role-based authorization (SuperAdmin / Admin / BusinessOwner / Customer), OTP verification, and immutable audit logs.

Technology Stack

Table 5.1 — Backend Technology Stack

## 5.2 Onion Architecture

Talentree implements the **Onion Architecture** pattern to achieve separation of concerns, dependency inversion, and domain-driven design principles. This architecture ensures the business domain remains independent of infrastructure concerns such as databases, frameworks, or external APIs. Every dependency arrow in the solution points *inward* — outer layers depend on inner contracts, never the reverse.

### 5.2.1 Architecture Principles

* **Dependency Inversion:** All dependencies point inward toward the domain core. Infrastructure depends on the domain, never the reverse.  
* **Domain-Centric Design:** Business logic resides in the Core layer, isolated from technical implementation details such as EF Core or HTTP.  
* **Testability:** Each layer can be tested independently through interface abstractions (`IUnitOfWork`, `IGenericRepository<T>`).  
* **Technology Agnostic Core:** `Talentree.Core` contains zero references to Entity Framework, ASP.NET, or any external library.

Figure 5.1 below illustrates the four concentric layers and their dependency direction.

![][image23]  
*Figure 5.1 — Onion Architecture layers in the Talentree backend solution* 

### 5.2.2 Domain Layer (Talentree.Core)

The innermost layer contains business entities, value objects, domain contracts, and specification classes. This layer has **zero external dependencies** — no NuGet package references to Entity Framework, ASP.NET, or any third-party library. All other layers depend on Core, never the reverse.

Key Entities (52 total)

![][image24]

Specification Pattern

Talentree uses the **Specification Pattern** to encapsulate query logic away from repositories and services. Specifications define filtering, ordering, pagination, and eager-loading as composable, testable objects that are evaluated by a `SpecificationsEvaluator<T>`.

![][image25]

*Listing 5.1 — Specification pattern example: admin product query with filtering, sorting, and pagination* 

### 5.2.3 Application Layer (Talentree.Service)

This layer contains business logic implementation, DTOs, AutoMapper profiles, and service orchestration. Services coordinate between repositories and external services (Stripe, AI microservice, SignalR). The layer also hosts the RabbitMQ consumer background services that react to domain events and trigger AI model calls asynchronously.

### 

### 5.2.4 Infrastructure Layer (Talentree.Repository)

This layer implements data access, database context configuration, EF Core migrations, and the Generic Repository pattern. The `TalentreeDbContext` applies a global soft-delete query filter dynamically to all entities that implement `ISoftDelete`, and enforces immutability of audit logs and SuperAdmin protection inside an overridden `SaveChangesAsync()`.

### 

### 

### 

### 

### 5.2.5 Presentation Layer (Talentree.API)

The outermost layer exposes HTTP endpoints, handles request/response serialization, applies authentication middleware, enforces rate limiting, and provides real-time SignalR hubs. Controllers are thin orchestrators — they validate the incoming request, call the appropriate service method, and wrap the result in a standardized `ApiResponse<T>` envelope before returning.

![][image26]

### 5.2.6 Advantages of Onion Architecture in Talentree

* **Testability:** Business logic can be unit-tested without a database. `IUnitOfWork` and `IGenericRepository<T>` can be mocked independently for each service.  
* **Maintainability:** Changes to infrastructure (e.g., switching from SQL Server to PostgreSQL) do not affect domain logic or service contracts.  
* **Domain Protection:** Database schema changes do not cascade into business rules. EF Core configurations are fully isolated in `Talentree.Repository`.  
* **Scalability:** New feature domains (e.g., the Admin AI Proxy) are added as controller \+ service \+ contract slices without modifying existing layers.  
* **Security Enforcement:** The `TalentreeDbContext.SaveChangesAsync()` override enforces SuperAdmin protection and audit log immutability at the database layer — independent of any service calling it.

## 5.3 Backend Project Structure

The solution is organized into four C\# projects, each representing one Onion Architecture layer. A fifth implicit component is the set of background-hosted RabbitMQ consumers inside `Talentree.Service` that bridge domain events to the AI microservice asynchronously.

Talentree's API follows REST architectural constraints strictly — using HTTP methods semantically, organizing resources hierarchically, and returning consistent JSON responses through a standardized `ApiResponse<T>` wrapper. All endpoints require a valid JWT bearer token in the `Authorization` header except for public authentication routes.

5.5 Database Design 

5.5.1 Database Architecture 

Talentree uses **Microsoft SQL Server** as its primary relational database, managed through **Entity Framework Core 8** with a Code-First approach. The database schema is fully version-controlled through EF Core Migrations, enabling reproducible schema evolution across development, staging, and production environments. The database is hosted on **Azure SQL Database** in production and connects via separate connection strings for each environment.

The schema is organized into functional domains matching the application's Onion Architecture layers. All entities inherit from one of two base classes — `BaseEntity` (with an integer primary key) or `AuditableEntity` (which adds `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`, `CreatedBy`, and `UpdatedBy` fields). Entities that support logical deletion implement the `ISoftDelete` interface, which adds `IsDeleted`, `DeletedAt`, and `DeletedBy` — with a global query filter applied automatically in `TalentreeDbContext` to hide soft-deleted records from all queries by default.

*Listing 5.6 — Base entity hierarchy: BaseEntity, AuditableEntity, and ISoftDelete interface*

5.6 Entity Framework Core

5.6.1 Code-First Approach

Talentree adopts the **Code-First** approach of Entity Framework Core, where the database schema is entirely derived from C\# class definitions rather than being designed first in a database management tool. This keeps the schema under version control alongside the application code, enables team collaboration through migrations, and provides a type-safe, object-oriented way to interact with the database.

Entity configurations are defined using the **Fluent API** inside individual `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>`classes located in `Talentree.Repository/Data/Configurations/`. These classes are auto-discovered at startup by `modelBuilder.ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly()`, keeping `TalentreeDbContext` clean and maintainable.

*Listing 5.7 — TalentreeDbContext: Code-First DbSets and auto-configuration discovery* 

Global Soft-Delete Query Filter

One of the most important cross-cutting concerns in the Code-First model is the automatic application of a global soft-delete query filter. During `OnModelCreating`, the context iterates over all entity types and — if they implement `ISoftDelete` — dynamically registers a `Where(e => e.IsDeleted == false)` filter. This filter applies to all LINQ queries automatically, without requiring developers to add it manually in every service. Admin queries that need to see deleted records call `EnableIgnoreQueryFilters()` on their specification.

5.6.2 Migrations

EF Core Migrations provide a structured, incremental approach to evolving the database schema over time. Talentree maintains **35 migration files** spanning the full development lifecycle from the initial authentication system in January 2026 to the final platform settings and chatbot tables added in June 2026\. Each migration is a pair of timestamped C\# files: the migration itself (containing `Up()` and `Down()` methods) and a designer snapshot.

Table 5.12 — Selected EF Core Migration Timeline

5.6.3 LINQ Queries

Talentree uses LINQ (Language Integrated Query) extensively for data retrieval and transformation. Queries are constructed within Specification classes and executed via the Generic Repository, ensuring consistent EF Core query patterns across all 25+ service classes. Key LINQ practices used include:

* **AsNoTracking():** Applied to all read-only queries to improve performance by disabling EF Core change tracking.  
* **Include() / ThenInclude():** Eager loading of related navigation properties to avoid N+1 query problems.  
* **Skip / Take:** Server-side pagination applied through specifications, never loading full table contents.  
* **Select projections:** Used in analytics to project aggregate values (e.g., average view duration, total revenue) directly in the SQL query.  
* **CountAsync():** Separate count query for pagination metadata; EF Core optimizes this by ignoring Include and OrderBy clauses automatically.

5.6.4 Repository Pattern

The Repository Pattern is a core architectural element in Talentree's data access layer. It abstracts the data persistence mechanism from the business logic, ensuring services interact with a clean interface contract rather than directly calling EF Core APIs. This promotes testability — services can be unit-tested with mock repositories — and enforces single-responsibility principles throughout the codebase.

5.6.4.1 GenericRepository\<T\>

The `GenericRepository<T>` class provides a unified, type-safe data access implementation for all domain entities. It exposes basic CRUD operations plus specification-based query methods, and delegates query construction to the `SpecificationsEvaluator<T>`. All read operations use `AsNoTracking()` for performance; write operations only mark entities in the change tracker without persisting — persistence is the responsibility of the Unit of Work.

5.6.4.2 IUnitOfWork

The **Unit of Work** pattern coordinates multiple repository operations into a single database transaction. All service classes receive `IUnitOfWork` through dependency injection. Repository instances are created lazily and cached in a dictionary keyed by the entity type name, ensuring the same `DbContext` instance (and therefore the same transaction) is shared across all repositories within a single request scope.

*Listing 5.9 — UnitOfWork: lazy repository caching and atomic transaction commit* 

5.6.4.3 Specification Pattern

Specifications are composable query objects that encapsulate filtering, sorting, eager-loading, and pagination logic. Each specification is a concrete class extending `BaseSpecifications<T>`, which holds all query criteria as typed expressions. The `SpecificationsEvaluator<T>` then builds the final `IQueryable<T>` by applying all criteria in sequence.

The `ISpecifications<T>` interface defines the complete contract: a `Criteria` expression (the WHERE clause), typed `Includes`, string-based `IncludeStrings` for deep navigation (e.g. `"Items.RawMaterial.Supplier"`), `OrderBy` / `OrderByDescending` expressions, pagination parameters (`Skip`, `Take`), and an `IgnoreQueryFilters` flag for admin queries that need to see soft-deleted records.

5.6.5 Entity Save Interceptor (Audit Interceptor) 

A persistent challenge in multi-user web platforms is ensuring that every data modification is traceable to the user who performed it and the exact time it occurred, without burdening each individual service method with repetitive bookkeeping code. Talentree addresses this through an **Entity Framework Core Save Interceptor** — the AuditInterceptor class — which intercepts every database write operation at the EF Core pipeline level and automatically populates audit fields across all eligible entities.

As illustrated in Figure 5.4, the interceptor integrates at the persistence pipeline, between the application service layer and the database. Because it operates at the EF Core interceptor hook rather than in application code, it is entirely transparent to callers: a service such as ProductService or CustomerOrderService simply calls \_unitOfWork.CompleteAsync() and the interceptor fires automatically, requiring no additional code in each service.

Class Design and Registration

The AuditInterceptor inherits from EF Core's built-in SaveChangesInterceptor abstract class and overrides both SavingChanges() (synchronous) and SavingChangesAsync() (asynchronous), ensuring the audit logic fires regardless of which overload is invoked. It is registered as a *Scoped* service in the application's DI container and injected directly into the TalentreeDbContext constructor, which then passes it to EF Core's interceptor pipeline via DbContextOptionsBuilder.AddInterceptors(). This design makes the interceptor available to every database context instance within the same HTTP request.

The current authenticated user's identity is resolved through IHttpContextAccessor, which surfaces the ASP.NET Core HttpContext for the current request. The interceptor extracts the NameIdentifier claim value — the user's GUID identifier — and assigns it to all audit fields populated within that request.

Audit Field Population Logic

The core logic resides in the private UpdateAuditFields(DbContext? context) method. It iterates the EF Core Change Tracker entries twice: once for entities inheriting from AuditableEntity, and once for entities implementing ISoftDelete that are in the Deleted state.

For AuditableEntity entries, the interceptor distinguishes between *Added* and *Modified* states. On *Added*, it writes CreatedAt and CreatedBy. On *Modified*, it writes UpdatedAt and UpdatedBy, and critically it marks CreatedAt and CreatedBy as IsModified \= false — this prevents EF Core from overwriting the original creation metadata even if the properties are accidentally set elsewhere in application code.

*Listing 5.2 — AuditInterceptor.UpdateAuditFields() core logic (AuditInterceptor.cs)*

The soft-delete branch intercepts any entity in the Deleted state that implements ISoftDelete. Instead of allowing EF Core to emit a DELETE SQL statement, the interceptor changes the tracking state to Modified and sets IsDeleted \= true, DeletedAt, and DeletedBy. This interception happens transparently: service code simply calls Repository.Delete(entity), and the interceptor ensures the physical row is never removed from the database.

In addition to the audit interceptor, TalentreeDbContext overrides SaveChanges() and SaveChangesAsync() to call an additional guard method, EnforceImmutabilityAndSuperAdminProtection(). This method throws an InvalidOperationException if any attempt is made to modify or delete a UserActionLog or LoginHistory record — both of which are designated as *immutable audit records*. It also prevents the last active SuperAdmin from being deactivated, deleted, or demoted, providing a data-integrity safety net at the persistence layer.

Table 5.15 — AuditableEntity and ISoftDelete Fields

5.6.6 Soft Delete & Global Query Filters

Physical deletion of database rows creates irreversible data loss and breaks referential integrity, complicates auditing, and prevents data recovery in case of accidental or malicious operations. Talentree therefore implements **Soft Delete** across all entities where historical data integrity is essential. Under this strategy, a record is never physically removed from the database; instead, it is flagged as logically deleted by setting IsDeleted \= true, populated automatically by the AuditInterceptor described in Section 5.6.5.

The ISoftDelete Interface

The contract for soft-deletable entities is defined in the ISoftDelete interface in Talentree.Core.Entities.BaseEntity. Any entity class that implements this interface gains the three fields shown in Table 5.15 above. As shown in the entities that implement this pattern, classes such as Product, Category, Supplier, RawMaterial, SupportTicket, BusinessOwnerProfile, KnowledgeArticle, and FAQ all participate in soft deletion, which covers all domain entities where data loss would be unacceptable.

*Listing 5.3 — ISoftDelete interface and an implementing entity (BaseEntity.cs, Product.cs)* 

Global Query Filter Application

The critical companion to the soft-delete write mechanism is ensuring that soft-deleted records are invisible to all read queries. Talentree achieves this through EF Core's **Global Query Filters**, configured inside TalentreeDbContext.OnModelCreating() via the private ApplyGlobalFilters(ModelBuilder modelBuilder) method.

The implementation uses reflection to iterate over all entity types registered in the EF Core model. For each type that implements ISoftDelete, it dynamically constructs a LINQ filter expression equivalent to entity \=\> entity.IsDeleted \== false using the .NET Expressions API, then applies it via entityType.SetQueryFilter(filterExpression). This technique is superior to manually adding .Where(x \=\> \!x.IsDeleted) in every repository query, as it ensures the filter is applied globally and cannot be accidentally omitted by developers writing new query methods.

*Listing 5.4 — Dynamic global query filter application (TalentreeDbContext.cs)*

*Listing 5.4 — Dynamic global query filter application (TalentreeDbContext.cs)*

The result is that every LINQ query executed through any Repository\<T\> where T implements ISoftDelete automatically receives a SQL WHERE IsDeleted \= 0 clause appended by EF Core before execution. The soft-deleted rows remain in the database and are accessible to administrative queries that bypass EF Core (e.g., direct SQL reporting queries) or through EF Core's IgnoreQueryFilters() API, which is used in certain administrative recovery scenarios.

5.7 Authentication & Authorization

5.7.1 JWT Authentication

Talentree implements **JSON Web Token (JWT)** authentication via the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer` package. Upon successful login, the server issues a short-lived access token (JWT) and a long-lived refresh token. The access token contains the user's ID, role claims, and standard JWT metadata. Every subsequent API request must include this token in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

The JWT is configured with strict validation parameters: issuer, audience, signing key, and lifetime are all validated. The `ClockSkew` is set to `TimeSpan.Zero` to eliminate the default 5-minute clock drift tolerance, ensuring tokens expire at the exact configured time. An `OnTokenValidated` event callback additionally checks that the user account is still active — if the user has been deactivated or suspended after token issuance, the token is immediately rejected.

Refresh Token Flow

Talentree implements a **Refresh Token Rotation** strategy. When the access token expires, the client sends the refresh token to the `/api/account/refresh-token` endpoint. The server validates the refresh token from the `RefreshTokens` table, invalidates the used token (preventing replay attacks), and issues a new access token / refresh token pair. This approach maintains user sessions without requiring re-login while limiting the attack window of compromised access tokens.

5.7.2 Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)

Talentree uses ASP.NET Core's **Role-Based Authorization** via `[Authorize(Roles = "...")]` attributes on controllers and actions. Roles are seeded into the `AspNetRoles` table at application startup by `DbInitializer`. The role hierarchy defines distinct permission boundaries as documented in Section 5.5.1.

Table 5.13 — RBAC Role Definitions and Authorization Examples

5.7.3 Password Hashing & Security

Passwords are never stored in plain text. ASP.NET Identity uses **PBKDF2 with HMAC-SHA256** (128-bit salt, 256-bit subkey, 100,000 iterations by default) for password hashing — an adaptive algorithm designed to be computationally expensive to resist brute-force attacks. A custom `DynamicPasswordValidator` is registered as a transient service that enforces configurable password strength rules fetched from `SecuritySettings` at runtime.

Additional security measures include OTP (One-Time Password) verification for email-based actions, account lockout after configurable failed login attempts (`SecuritySettings.MaxLoginAttempts`), and session revocation capability (admins can force-logout any user by invalidating all refresh tokens associated with that account).

5.7.4 Protected Routes & Policies

All API routes except authentication endpoints (`/api/auth/**`, `/api/account/register`) require a valid JWT bearer token. The middleware pipeline enforces authentication before authorization: `UseAuthentication()` → `UseAuthorization()`. The SignalR hub endpoint (`/hubs/notification`) is protected with `[Authorize]` and extracts the JWT from the WebSocket upgrade query string (`?access_token=<token>`) when HTTP headers are not available. Rate limiting is applied to AI proxy endpoints via the `AdminAi` fixed-window policy (20 requests per minute).

5.7.5 Refresh Token Management & Session Revocation

JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are stateless by design: once issued, a JWT is valid until its expiry without any server-side knowledge. Short-lived access tokens (15 minutes by default in Talentree) mitigate the risk of token theft, but they require a mechanism for seamless session renewal without forcing the user to re-authenticate on every expiry. Talentree implements **Refresh Token Rotation** — a widely adopted security pattern — through the TokenService and AuthService classes.

Token Generation and Storage

When a user successfully authenticates (via standard login, two-factor verification, forced password change, or social login), the AuthService generates two tokens: a short-lived JWT access token and a long-lived opaque refresh token. The refresh token is generated as a 64-byte cryptographically random value produced by System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator and returned to the client as a Base64 string.

The raw refresh token is **never stored in the database**. Instead, it is immediately hashed using SHA-256 before persistence. The TokenService.HashToken() method converts the plain token string to its hash digest, which is then stored in the RefreshToken entity's TokenHash column. This means that even if the database is compromised, attackers cannot use the stored hashes to forge valid sessions — a hash cannot be reversed to the original token value.

*Listing 5.5 — Refresh token generation and SHA-256 hashing (TokenService.cs)*

RefreshToken Entity

The RefreshToken entity inherits from BaseEntity and stores the minimum information required for validation and revocation. The IsActive computed property encapsulates the validity logic in a single, testable expression, making it impossible for service code to forget to check both conditions simultaneously.

Token Refresh Workflow and Rotation

As illustrated in Figure 5.5, when the client sends a token refresh request, the AuthService.RefreshTokenAsync() method first hashes the provided token, then queries the database for a matching RefreshToken record using a specification. If found and IsActive returns true, a new access token and a new refresh token are issued. Critically, the old refresh token is immediately revoked by setting its RevokedAt timestamp — this is the Refresh Token *Rotation* strategy. A client that replays an old refresh token (after it has already been used) will find it revoked, preventing replay attacks.

*Figure 5.5 — Refresh Token Rotation Flow with revocation on reuse*

Session Revocation

Session revocation is the ability to immediately invalidate a user's active session, forcing re-authentication. Talentree supports this at multiple levels. During **logout**, AuthService.LogoutAsync() locates the refresh token by its hash and sets RevokedAt, making the session instantly invalid. During **password reset**, the service queries all active refresh tokens for the affected user via the ActiveRefreshTokensForUserSpecification and revokes every one of them in a single transaction — ensuring that a password reset always terminates all existing sessions. During **admin password reset**, the same bulk-revocation pattern is applied through AdminService. This comprehensive revocation design means there is no residual window of access after a security-critical event.

The access token's lifetime is configurable per user role. For administrators, the TokenService reads the SecuritySettings.SessionTimeoutInMinutes value from the database, allowing the platform's Super Admin to tighten or relax the session duration without redeployment.

Table 5.17 — Refresh Token & Session Management API Endpoints

5.7.6 One-Time Password (OTP) Verification

Talentree uses a **database-backed One-Time Password (OTP)** system to secure three distinct user flows: email address verification after registration, password reset, and two-factor authentication (2FA). All three share the same underlying OtpCode entity and generation infrastructure, differentiated only by the OtpPurpose enumeration value.

OtpCode Entity Design

The OtpCode entity stores all information required to validate a code while making replay attacks practically impossible. As shown in Listing 5.6, the entity contains the code itself, the purpose for which it was issued, lifecycle timestamps, and a usage flag. The two computed properties — IsExpired and IsValid — encapsulate validation logic at the model level, ensuring consistent enforcement across all service methods that verify codes.

*Listing 5.6 — OtpCode entity and OtpPurpose enumeration (OtpCode.cs)*

*Listing 5.6 — OtpCode entity and OtpPurpose enumeration (OtpCode.cs)*

Code Generation and Delivery

OTP codes are six-digit numeric strings generated by the `GenerateOtpCode()` private helper in `AuthService`, which uses `Random.Shared.Next(100000, 999999)` to produce a uniform random integer in the six-digit range. The code is saved to the database with a five-minute expiry window via `SaveOtpCodeAsync(userId, code, purpose)`, then dispatched to the user's registered email address by the `EmailService.SendOtpAsync()` method. The delivery of the code by email acts as the first factor of identity verification, since only the legitimate account holder should have access to the registered inbox.

OTP Verification Flows

All three OTP verification flows follow the same structural pattern, as illustrated in Figure 5.6. The service queries the `OtpCode` repository using an `OtpCodeSpecification` that filters by user ID, the submitted code string, and the expected purpose. If no record is found or the record's `IsValid` computed property returns `false` (either already used or expired), the operation is rejected. If valid, the service proceeds with the purpose-specific action and immediately sets `IsUsed = true` with `UsedAt = DateTime.UtcNow`, preventing any subsequent reuse of the same code even within its five-minute window.

Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)

Two-factor authentication is triggered by the LoginAsync() method under two conditions: when the user has personally opted into 2FA by setting AppUser.IsTwoFactorEnabled \= true, or when the platform administrator has enabled the SecuritySettings.RequireTwoFactorForAdmins flag, which enforces 2FA for all admin-role users regardless of their individual setting.

When 2FA is triggered, the login flow pauses: an OTP of purpose TwoFactorAuth is generated and emailed, and a partial AuthResponseDto with RequiresTwoFactor \= true is returned to the client rather than a full token pair. The client is expected to redirect the user to a 2FA verification screen and submit the six-digit code to /api/auth/verify-2fa. Upon successful verification, VerifyTwoFactorAsync() marks the OTP as used and proceeds to issue the JWT access token and refresh token.

A special Super Admin emergency bypass mechanism is also implemented: if the OTP code submitted matches the SeedData:SuperAdminEmergency2FaBypassCode configuration value, the OTP database check is skipped and authentication proceeds. This mechanism exists to prevent a Super Admin from being permanently locked out of the system if the email delivery service is unavailable. All bypass usages are recorded in the audit log with the specific action label *"Emergency 2FA Bypass Used"* for full accountability.

Invalidation of Stale Codes on Resend

When a user requests a new verification email (e.g., the original OTP expired or was not received), the `ResendVerificationEmailAsync()` method explicitly queries all existing unused, non-expired OTP codes for that user and the same purpose, and marks each as `IsUsed = true` before generating a fresh code. This ensures that multiple valid codes cannot coexist for the same user and purpose — preventing scenarios where an attacker who intercepts an old code can still use it after a resend.

5.8 Real-Time Communication with SignalR

Talentree integrates **ASP.NET Core SignalR** to deliver real-time, bi-directional communication between the server and connected clients. SignalR automatically selects the best transport protocol available — WebSockets (preferred), Server-Sent Events, or Long Polling — providing a seamless real-time experience across all browsers and network environments. The hub endpoint is registered at `/hubs/notification` and is protected by JWT authentication.

5.8.1 Notification System

The notification system is built around a **user-group targeting strategy**. On connection, each authenticated user is added to a personal SignalR group named `User_{userId}`. Server-side services send targeted notifications by broadcasting to this group via `IHubContext<NotificationHub>`, which is injected into the `HubService` wrapper class.

The `HubService` exposes four methods consumed by all service classes across the application: `SendNotificationToUserAsync` (targeted single-user push), `UpdateUnreadCountAsync` (real-time badge counter update), `SendNotificationToUsersAsync` (multi-user bulk push), and `SendToAllAsync` (platform-wide broadcast for system announcements).

*Listing 5.11 — HubService: wraps IHubContext for use by the application service layer* 

5.8.2 Real-Time Order Updates

Order status transitions trigger real-time SignalR notifications to the relevant Business Owner and Customer. When an admin updates an order status or a production request progresses through its workflow, the service layer calls `IHubService.SendNotificationToUserAsync()` to instantly push the update to the affected user's browser without requiring a page refresh. The notification payload includes the entity type, entity ID, new status, and a human-readable message — allowing the frontend to update the relevant UI components in place.

Table 5.14 — SignalR Events and Their Triggers

Figure 5.10 illustrates the full SignalR communication lifecycle — from client connection and JWT authentication through the group assignment and real-time event delivery flow.

*Figure 5.10 — SignalR live communication workflow: WebSocket connection lifecycle, JWT validation, group assignment, and event delivery* 

Hub Configuration

The SignalR hub is configured in `Program.cs` with production-grade settings: a 15-second keep-alive interval to maintain WebSocket connections through load balancers and proxies, a 30-second client timeout to detect and clean up stale connections, and a 10 MB maximum message size to accommodate notification payloads with embedded content. Detailed error messages are enabled only in the development environment to avoid exposing internal details in production.

5.9 Payment Gateway Integration

5.9.1 Stripe Integration

Talentree integrates **Stripe** as its primary payment gateway for processing financial transactions between platform participants. Stripe was selected for its robust API, PCI DSS compliance certification, comprehensive webhook system, and native .NET SDK support. The integration enables two distinct payment flows: Material Order payments (Business Owners paying suppliers for raw materials) and Production Request payments (Business Owners paying Talentree for custom production services).

The Stripe configuration is stored securely in `appsettings.json` (with secrets in Azure Key Vault for production) under three keys: `Stripe:SecretKey` (server-side API key), `Stripe:PublishableKey` (frontend key for Stripe.js), and `Stripe:WebhookSecret` (for webhook signature verification). The `IPaymentService` interface abstracts all Stripe SDK calls from the controller layer, maintaining clean Onion Architecture boundaries.

Table 5.15 — Stripe Integration Configuration

5.9.2 Payment Processing Workflow

Talentree implements the **PaymentIntent** model recommended by Stripe, which provides strong client authentication (SCA) compliance and supports payment method confirmation on the frontend using Stripe.js. The workflow follows a clear four-step sequence as illustrated in Figure 5.12 and documented below.

*Figure 5.12 — Stripe PaymentIntent lifecycle: from checkout through webhook-driven payment confirmation*

As illustrated in Figure 5.12, the payment flow begins when the Business Owner initiates a checkout (Step 1 — creating the order record). Step 2 calls the `create-intent` endpoint, which invokes the Stripe SDK server-side to create a `PaymentIntent` object with the exact amount and currency. Stripe returns a `clientSecret` (Step 4\) which the frontend uses to call `stripe.confirmCardPayment()` (Step 5). Stripe processes the card (Step 6\) and fires a `payment_intent.succeeded` webhook event to the backend (Step 7), which updates the database payment status (Step 8). This asynchronous webhook approach ensures payment confirmation is server-verified and never relies on client-reported success.

5.9.3 Refund Management

Talentree implements a structured refund workflow accessible from both customer and business owner perspectives. Customers can submit a `RefundRequest` against a specific order item through `POST /api/customer/orders/{id}/items/{itemId}/refund`. Business owners can review pending refund requests and respond (approve or reject) through dedicated endpoints. When a refund is approved, the `IPaymentService` calls `Stripe.RefundService.CreateAsync()` with the original `PaymentIntentId`, processing the reversal directly to the cardholder's account. Refund status transitions are tracked through the `RefundRequests` table with an immutable audit trail.

5.9.4 Webhook Handling

The Stripe webhook endpoint at `POST /api/payment/webhook` is configured as `[AllowAnonymous]` since it is called directly by Stripe's servers, not by authenticated users. Security is enforced through **Stripe webhook signature verification**: the raw request body is read as a string (buffered before authentication middleware) and passed along with the `Stripe-Signature` header to `EventUtility.ConstructEvent()` using the `WebhookSecret`. Any request with an invalid or missing signature returns HTTP 400\. The event handler follows a **idempotency strategy** by storing processed `MessageId` values in the `ProcessedMessages` table, preventing duplicate processing if Stripe retries delivery.

	

*Listing 5.12 — Stripe webhook receiver with signature-based security and idempotent event handling*

5.10 Business Services & Core Workflows

The business-service layer is the operational heart of the Talentree backend. It is implemented as a collection of focused, single-responsibility C\# service classes located in the *Talentree.Service* project. Each service encapsulates a distinct business domain, depending only on the Unit-of-Work pattern and AutoMapper for data persistence and transformation, thereby keeping business rules cleanly separated from infrastructure concerns. The following subsections document each major service, the workflows it orchestrates, and the REST API endpoints it exposes through the corresponding ASP.NET Core controllers.

5.10.1 Product Management & Approval Workflow

Product management in Talentree follows a mandatory review cycle before a product is visible to customers. The ProductService class implements the complete product lifecycle for Business Owners, while the AdminService handles the administrative approval gate. The system enforces a strict status machine across four states: *Draft*, *PendingApproval*, *Approved*, and *Rejected*.

As illustrated in Figure 5.1, when a Business Owner submits a new product, the service first verifies that the owner's profile has an *Approved* status. It then validates that between one and five images are attached, each satisfying the 5 MB size ceiling and JPEG/PNG format constraint enforced by ImageService.IsValidImage(). After persisting the product entity, an asynchronous event is published to the ai.product RabbitMQ exchange so that the AI microservice can compute demand-score and quality metrics in the background without blocking the HTTP response.

*Figure 5.1 — Product Submission and Admin Approval Workflow*

*Figure 5.1 — Product Submission and Admin Approval Workflow*

An important business rule governs product editing: a product whose status is *Approved* is automatically reset to *PendingApproval* upon any update, ensuring that changes are reviewed by an administrator before re-publication. Products in the *PendingApproval* or *Rejected* states cannot be edited. Deletion is implemented as a soft-delete; the AuditInterceptor automatically sets IsDeleted \= true without removing the database record, preserving audit history.

5.10.2 Shopping Cart & Material Basket

Talentree operates two distinct basket abstractions that serve different user roles and purchasing contexts. The **Customer Shopping Cart** (CartService) allows end customers to accumulate finished products for checkout, while the **Material Basket** (MaterialBasketService) enables Business Owners to collect raw materials from approved suppliers prior to creating a production request.

Customer Shopping Cart

The CartService implements a lazy-creation pattern: when a customer performs their first cart operation, the service automatically provisions an empty CustomerCart entity linked to that customer's identity. Real-time stock validation is enforced at every add and update operation; if the requested quantity exceeds the product's current StockQuantity, the service immediately raises a BadRequestException with a descriptive message. Every successful add-to-cart action additionally publishes an interaction.log event to the AI service so that clickstream data can feed the recommendation engine.

Checkout pricing follows a simple, deterministic rule: orders with a subtotal below EGP 100 incur a flat EGP 10 shipping fee; orders at or above that threshold qualify for free shipping.

Material Basket

The material basket enforces supplier-defined constraints at the item level. Before accepting an add-item request, MaterialBasketService verifies that the requested quantity satisfies the raw material's MinimumOrderQuantity and does not exceed its available StockQuantity. If the same material already exists in the basket, the service increments the existing line item rather than creating a duplicate row, keeping basket management simple for the Business Owner.

Table 5.3 — Cart & Basket API Endpoints

5.10.3 Customer Order Processing

Order placement is the most transactionally critical workflow in the Talentree platform. The CustomerOrderService orchestrates a multi-step process that must complete atomically: cart validation, stock reservation, order creation, cart clearance, payment intent generation (for credit-card orders), and multi-party notification dispatch.

As shown in Figure 5.2, the service first validates the customer's active status. It then iterates over every cart item to confirm that sufficient stock exists. Product prices are *snapshotted* into the CustomerOrderItem entity at the moment of ordering, ensuring that subsequent price changes by the seller do not retroactively affect completed orders. Stock levels are decremented atomically within the same UnitOfWork.CompleteAsync() call that persists the order, preventing race-condition overselling.

*Figure 5.2 — Customer Order Placement Flow*

*Figure 5.2 — Customer Order Placement Flow*

Two payment methods are supported: *Cash on Delivery*, which moves the order directly to *Processing* status, and *Credit Card*, which sets it to *Pending* awaiting a Stripe PaymentIntent confirmation. Invoice generation is available through a dedicated endpoint that returns a minimal PDF byte stream for the customer's records. Customers may cancel orders that are still in the *Pending* state; the service automatically restores stock levels for all cancelled items.

Table 5.4 — Customer Order API Endpoints

5.10.4 Business Owner Payout Management

The PayoutService manages the full lifecycle of earnings withdrawal requests. Business Owners accumulate a running balance stored as the BalanceAfter field on their most recent Transaction ledger entry. When a Business Owner wishes to withdraw funds, they submit a CreatePayoutRequestDto containing the desired amount, bank name, account holder name, account identifier, and optional SWIFT/routing code.

The service enforces two inviolable business rules before persisting the request:

When an administrator marks a payout as *Completed*, the service creates a new Transaction ledger entry of type Payout with a negative Amount (representing a debit), and the new running BalanceAfter is computed and persisted. Immediately after, an ai.anomaly event is published to the AI microservice, which applies its Isolation Forest model to flag any statistical anomalies in the transaction.

Table 5.5 — Payout Management API Endpoints

5.10.5 Customer Support & Ticket Management

The SupportService implements a fully threaded, attachment-capable helpdesk system. Business Owners open support tickets categorised by topic (e.g., Payment, Product, Technical), and administrators manage resolution through a structured status lifecycle: *Open → InProgress → AwaitingReply → Resolved → Closed*.

Upon ticket creation, the service generates a deterministic, human-readable ticket number in the format TKT-YYYY-NNNNN (e.g., TKT-2026-00042), where the sequence counter resets annually. Simultaneously, the ai.triage event is published so the AI service can automatically predict the ticket's priority category, reducing the manual triage workload for the support team.

Each ticket and each message within it may carry up to three file attachments. The service enforces a 10 MB per-file ceiling and restricts accepted MIME types to JPEG, PNG, GIF, PDF, and plain text. Files are stored through the FileService into the wwwroot/uploads/support-tickets directory. When a Business Owner adds a new message to a ticket that had been *Resolved*, the ticket is automatically reopened to *Open* status, preventing issues from being silently ignored.

5.10.6 Complaint Management

The complaint system provides an authenticated mechanism for any platform user to formally report another user or content-related issue. The ComplaintController delegates all business logic to the UserManagementService, which handles persistence and the associated notification flow. A key design decision is that complaint creation is accessible to any authenticated user regardless of role, enabling both customers and Business Owners to file reports.

Administrators review submitted complaints through the AdminComplaintController, which exposes listing and resolution endpoints. Each complaint is linked to the ReportedByUserId extracted from the authenticated JWT, preventing anonymous or impersonated submissions.

5.10.7 Knowledge Base Management

The Knowledge Base is a self-service content library designed to help Business Owners learn platform features and grow their businesses. The KnowledgeService serves articles to Business Owners, while the AdminKnowledgeService handles article authoring and analytics for administrators.

Articles support rich metadata: ContentType (e.g., Article, Video, Guide), Category (e.g., GettingStarted, Marketing, Inventory), comma-delimited tags, an optional ExternalUrl for embedded videos, and a FileUrl for downloadable attachments. View counts are incremented atomically each time an article is fetched by ID, providing the raw data for the analytics dashboard.
